sam_support: FYI customer reporting intermittent embeddings "dimension mismatch" errors and simultaneous tail-latency spikes on /v1/embeddings. Happens in bursts around traffic spikes, looks correlated with dynamic batching. Customer sees errors like 'Invalid embedding length: expected 1024, got 768'.

chris_ml: Can you paste a minimal request they used + the X-Request-ID from the failing requests? Also which model they hit and whether they pinned a model route?

sam_support: Here's the curl they ran (redacted):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-super-1024","input":["a short sentence","another one"]}'
```

And sample error from our gateway logs: `embed-err: request_id=RID-9b3f status=400 msg="Invalid embedding length: expected=1024 got=768" route=customer-us-west-1`

eng_oncall: Two quick hypotheses: 1) client is intermittently hitting a different model variant (e.g. embed-lite-768) due to routing/fallbacks; 2) dynamic batching is coalescing requests from different model ids and an upstream transformer variant returns 768 vectors while our validator expects 1024.

Try these repro/triage steps:
- confirm request `model` field consistently set by client (no model aliasing)
- check route config: `redwoodctl routes get --customer <cid>` (look for model aliases / fallbacks)
- dump batcher config for the node: `curl http://batcher-local:9090/config` -> look for `max_batch_size`, `coalescing_window_ms`, and `allow_mixed_model_batches`

Example batcher config snippet we want to see: 
```json
{
  "max_batch_size": 64,
  "coalescing_window_ms": 8,
  "allow_mixed_model_batches": false,
  "dynamic_batching": {"enabled": true}
}
```

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: runtime/batcher v3.14 rolled @ 2026-03-22T18:41:02Z by ci-pipeline (sha: a1b2c3).

chris_ml: If the batcher is configured to allow mixed-model batches (or if model pins are not enforced in the routing layer) that would explain mismatch. Short-term experiment: set `allow_mixed_model_batches=false` and reduce `coalescing_window_ms` to 1-2ms or set `max_batch_size` to a small value (e.g., 8) to see if the 768/1024 mix disappears and tail p95 improves. Also ask customer to pin `model=embed-super-1024` explicitly and retry.

sam_support: Did an A/B with them: disabling dynamic batching (`dynamic_batching.enabled=false`) removed the 400s immediately and p95 tail dropped from ~1.2s to ~220ms, but throughput degraded ~18%. Customer accepted short-term tradeoff.

eng_oncall: Good repro. For a permanent fix we'll want:
- ensure routing layer enforces model id compatibility (no cross-mixing in batchers)
- add a validator in batch assembly to reject mixed-dim batches and return 409 so client gets deterministic error earlier (instead of downstream 400s)
- instrument batcher metrics: `mixed_model_batch_count`, `mixed_dim_rejects`, `coalescing_window_hist`

ops_lead: Can you capture the tracer IDs and a sample raw payload for one of the mixed failures and attach to ENG-INC-4721? Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/ENG-INC-4721 (please redact PII). Also include the batcher config from the node and the route dump.

chris_ml: I'll pick this up. Quick note to support: if you see regressions after our patch, we might want to roll back the canary (deploy-bot: see deploy above) and reopen dynamic batching with a stricter `allow_mixed_model_batches=false` guard.

sam_support: Thanks — I've uploaded logs + two sample request IDs to the ticket and informed the customer they're on a mitigation plan. :thumbsup: 

chris_ml: Assigned ENG-INC-4721 to runtime team, will follow up with a short postmortem and configuration changes.

eng_oncall: also adding an alert rule: fire if `mixed_model_batch_count > 0` for 2 consecutive minutes.

sam_support: closing loop with customer, will update if they see any more spikes. :white_check_mark:
